articles.title: Checking agent code against your intent
articles.summary: Coding agents write more code than anyone can read. Uncle Bob's answer is to stop reading. Mine is to get agents to write less code, and better code. Tools like Microsoft's NFV help with the better: they write down what a change is meant to do, have an agent prove the code does it, and let Lean or Dafny check the proof. What does such a proof tell you? That the code has the property. What can't it tell you? Whether the property was the right one. Can you stop reading the code? No. Figure 1. articles.title: Replaying an agent run and what it takes
articles.summary: Tether is a Rust harness that wraps an agent somebody else wrote. Every model call and tool call the agent makes goes through it, is checked against a policy, and is written to a trace. This is about one property of that trace: you can run the agent again from it, with no network and no cost, and get the same run. Not a similar run. The same events, equal field for field.
